data.description:
iter_agentsview_sessions (toolbench/sources.py:153) builds:

    argv = ["agentsview", "session", "list", "--json", "--limit", str(limit)]

The design doc (docs/2026-07-07-tool-benchmarks-design.md:57) mandates:

    agentsview session list ... --include-children --include-automated --include-one-shot --limit 500 --json

None of the three --include-* flags are passed. agentsview excludes one-shot, automated, and child sessions BY DEFAULT and announces it on stderr:

    Excluded 7494 sessions by default: 7433 one-shot, 61 automated.

sources.py checks only returncode and parses stdout, so the banner is discarded.

MEASURED (full cursor pagination, live archive, 2026-07-13):
  toolbench actual call (no flags):  3534 sessions
  design-mandated (all 3 includes): 11950 sessions
  SILENTLY EXCLUDED:                 8416  (70.4% of the archive)

WHY S35 CANNOT SEE IT: the loss is UPSTREAM of discovery. The Summary prints a
perfectly balanced 'Sessions discovered: 200 / scanned: 200 / skipped: 0' because
D is already truncated. This is the TB-21 family (unreconciled corpus loss) one
level further up: not skipped, never discovered.

CONSEQUENCE FOR S10 (the real damage): auto->raw fallback is NOT corpus-preserving.
Same agent, same --limit 50, only --index-source differs:
  raw:        50 scanned, 693 calls,  fingerprint d67c5c93fc1e67e7
  agentsview: 50 scanned, 4016 calls, fingerprint e432354b624ff485
A 5.8x call-density difference. The report names the fallback reason, which implies
a PROVENANCE change; it is actually a POPULATION change. Numbers measured across a
fallback boundary are not comparable, and S37 freeze pins a different population
depending on which index source was live.

FIX: pass --include-children --include-automated --include-one-shot in
iter_agentsview_sessions; surface agentsview stderr exclusion banner rather than
discarding it. Add a test asserting the argv carries all three flags, and an
index-source equivalence test (raw vs agentsview over the same project must agree
on the discovered session-id set).

Found by: operator smoke checkpoint CP2/CP3 (EVALUATION.md), 2026-07-13.
data.title: agentsview index path silently excludes 70% of the archive: --include-{children,automated,one-shot} never passed

data.body:
CORROBORATION FROM A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ORACLE (operator checkpoint CP7, 2026-07-13)

Cross-checking the S32 hermes cache ratio against the hermes profile databases
turned up the same under-discovery from a different direction -- and it is WORSE
for hermes than for claude, which makes it worse than TB-30 first described.

  hermes sessions in profile DBs (direct SELECT, 4 profiles):  996
  hermes sessions passive actually discovered (--limit 400):    99   (~10%)

Broken down by agentsview flag, --agent hermes:

  toolbench actual call (no flags):        99 sessions
  + --include-automated:                   99 sessions
  + --include-one-shot:                   500+ (still paginating)
  + all three includes:                   500+ (still paginating)

So hermes' missing ~900 sessions are almost entirely ONE-SHOT sessions -- hermes
runs heavily cron/automated/one-shot workloads (cf. 'cron_2d647784731c_...' ids in
'hermes sessions list'), and those are exactly what agentsview drops by default.

WHY THIS RAISES SEVERITY: the exclusion is NOT UNIFORM ACROSS AGENTS. claude is
sampled at one fraction of its archive; hermes at roughly 10% of its. This project
exists to COMPARE agents' tool efficiency. Any cross-agent number in the report --
the Agent Breakdown, the Tool Leaderboard, the S19 context-cost ranking -- is
currently computed over per-agent populations selected by wildly different sampling
fractions, with no disclosure. The comparison is not apples-to-apples, and nothing
in the report says so.

This also means the S32 caveat ratio itself is measured on a biased 10% slice:
  passive (scanned slice):        96 of 99  = 97.0%
  direct SELECT (all 996):       909 of 996 = 91.3%
The two agree closely enough to pass CP7, but the agreement is partly luck -- the
one-shot sessions passive never saw could have had a very different cache profile.

FIX (unchanged, but now higher priority): pass the three --include-* flags, and
surface per-agent discovered/total so a skewed sample is visible in the report
rather than invisible.

FIXED in PR #53 (branch fix/tb-30-31-agentsview-corpus-and-subagents).

All three --include-* flags are now passed. The stderr exclusion banner is no longer
discarded: it raises AgentsViewExclusionWarning, on the reasoning that we now opt into
every exclusion agentsview documents, so a banner means it dropped sessions we did NOT
ask it to drop.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY before fixing (live archive, full cursor pagination):
  toolbench actual call (no flags):  3536
  design-mandated (all 3 includes): 11955   -> 70.4% silently excluded. Confirmed.

The CP7 per-agent skew also reproduced, and is the real severity:
  claude 1934/8585 = 22.5% | hermes 99/977 = 10.1% | codex 90/173 = 52.0% | cursor 55/73 = 75.3%
A 7.4x spread in sampling fraction, in a project whose whole purpose is comparing agents.

THE FIX RESOLVES THE SKEW AT THE ROOT rather than merely disclosing it: every agent is now
discovered at 100% of its archive (bounded only by --limit). So the CP7 ask to 'surface
per-agent discovered/total' is no longer needed for THIS cause.

RESIDUAL, NOT ADDRESSED HERE: with --agent all and a --limit, the N most-recent sessions
can still be dominated by one agent. That is a uniform, visible truncation rather than a
hidden default exclusion -- a different and much milder problem. Worth its own ticket if
the operator wants per-agent discovered/total disclosed anyway.

SHIPPED WITH TB-31 DELIBERATELY. TB-30 alone would have made things worse: today
--include-children is absent, so children never enter the corpus and --exclude-subagents is
a HARMLESS no-op. Admitting children without fixing the filter turns it into a no-op that
fails to remove subagents that are now actually present, while the report still claims
'Subagents included: no'.

provenance.reason: Fix designed: three --include-* flags + parent-probe set difference for is_subagent
PR #53 open; 511 tests pass, ruff + mypy --strict clean; verified end-to-end on the live archive
